Replaced the unconditional client-as-owner and public-key-decryption explanations and separated obligatory ROPC prohibition (DARF NICHT) from the conditional implicit recommendation (SOLLTE NICHT). Preserved issuer-scoped subject identity, transaction-specific bindings, required claim presence and nonce, algorithm/key trust and the narrow Python profile; clarified browser-function grammar and kept Bit/Byte distinct.
limitations: AI technical and editorial review, not a native-speaker or human confirmation.
No live OP, network JWKS fetch, browser login, session-security audit or penetration test.
Mermaid source and HTML checked; visual diagram rendering was not inspected.
Four other OAuth/OIDC translations remain unreviewed and retain old content.
Publication verification pending.

meaning.note: Read the entire original Indonesian metadata/body and complete corrected Japanese source, revised all metadata and prose, and independently reread the full Indonesian revision. Compared authentication/authorization, four OAuth roles and grants, public/confidential clients, normative grant conditions, transaction-specific PKCE, browser redirects and code exchange, OIDC scope/token purposes, required claims and key trust, state/nonce/CSRF, expiry and optional refresh lifecycle. Matched all ten sequence messages, actors and notes. Structural and execution checks supplement full semantic reading.

terminology.note: Distinguished autentikasi/otorisasi, tanda tangan/enkripsi/dekripsi, klaim, penerbit/penerima, masa berlaku or kedaluwarsa versus pencabutan, klien konfidensial/publik and token akses/ID/pembaruan. Used peramban, pengikatan per transaksi, kredensial and string opak (opaque) rather than a literal blurred-string description. Corrected token decoding presented as login, mandatory refresh, encrypted signatures and public-key decryption, and the assumption that client credentials always makes the client the resource owner. Kept TIDAK BOLEH (MUST NOT) for ROPC distinct from conditional SEBAIKNYA TIDAK (SHOULD NOT) for implicit access-token responses. Preserved issuer-scoped sub identity, mandatory nonce/claims, trusted key acquisition, exact transaction bindings and the restricted Python profile. Explained sender constraints as cryptographic binding to the client presenting the token.

mathematics.note: Compared all three display formulas and their premises: S256 ASCII verifier input and unpadded Base64url, JWS ASCII signing input and algorithm-internal hashing, and expiry reformulation only when exp=iat+lifetime. First two formulas exactly match the source; only translated conditional text differs in the third. Extracted JavaScript passed the RFC vector; identical JWS and expiry expressions use independent source cryptography and boundary/counterexample checks.

code.note: Executed both extracted JavaScript and Python blocks per language using Node v22.14.0, PyJWT 2.15.1 and cryptography. JS checks covered 32-byte encoding and upper-bit retention, the RFC vector, valid lengths 43/128, twelve invalid inputs including trailing newlines, and returned S256 parameter binding. Each Python block passed 38 cases covering required claims, nonce, strict audience, azp, claim types, signature, algorithm none, issuer, expiry, nbf and transaction nonce arguments. AST and exact JavaScript equality checked. These are offline component fixtures, not a complete login or provider-conformance test.

terminology.note: Distinguished प्रमाणीकरण (authentication), प्राधिकरण (authorization), सत्यापन, हस्ताक्षर versus एन्क्रिप्शन/डिक्रिप्शन, गोपनीय versus सार्वजनिक क्लाइंट, जारीकर्ता versus प्राप्तकर्ता, and निरस्तीकरण versus समाप्ति. Used क्लेम, प्राधिकरण प्रयास, क्रेडेंशियल, बाइंडिंग and रिफ्रेश टोकन consistently, keeping बाइट distinct from बिट. Corrected the old encrypted-signature/public-key-decryption and decoding-as-login explanations, generic three-part JWT, mandatory-refresh and client-as-owner assumptions. Preserved the ROPC prohibition and conditional implicit recommendation, issuer-local sub identity, transaction-specific nonce/state/PKCE and the narrow Python profile. Explicitly states रिफ्रेश टोकन रद्द कर देने पर भी, पहले से जारी एक्सेस टोकन... so preexisting access-token validity is not confused with the timing before revocation. Explained sender constraints as cryptographic binding to the presenting client.
